hypotheses.justification: This assumption follows from the others. `G` is locally compact and `hH : IsClosed (H : Set G)`, so `IsClosed.locallyCompactSpace` (Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean) gives `LocallyCompactSpace H`. `[μH.IsHaarMeasure]` includes `IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μH`, so the instance `isLocallyFiniteMeasure_of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts` (Typeclasses/Finite.lean) gives `IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μH`. `H` is second countable as a subtype of `G`, so the instance `sigmaFinite_of_locallyFinite` (Typeclasses/SFinite.lean) gives `SigmaFinite μH`, hence `SFinite μH`. The statement elaborates without it, because `HaarQuotient.density` only needs the topology and measurable structure on G and a measure on H. In the proof it is used only by `measurable_density`, through `lintegral_prod_right'`. Adding `haveI : LocallyCompactSpace H := hH.locallyCompactSpace` at the start of the proof lets instance search supply it there. `lintegral_withDensity_eq_of_admissible` does not take `SFinite μH`. No degenerate case causes trouble, since the derivation holds for every closed subgroup H.
